name: chalette-dev
description: Chalette Command Room 2 dev skills, shared by Matthew and Erick: cr2-report, cr2-scrub, cr2-test, cr2-desk. v0.7.0 (2026-10-04): the Command Room 1 QA toolkit (16 skills) moved to Matthew's private chalette plugin; this plugin is Command Room 2 only. PRIOR HISTORY: Chalette internal dev & QA toolkit for Command Room. v0.6.0 (2026-10-04): the Command Room 2 dev skills join the toolkit so Matthew and Erick work the same way: cr2-report (file a bug or feature on ChaletteHQ/cr2), cr2-scrub (keep client, personal and money information out of the repo; private name lists stay in a gitignored config/scrub.local.json), cr2-test (supervised acceptance tests, results posted to the issue), cr2-desk (everything pending to build, in plain language, and a guided build brief). Operator-aware: Matthew decides routes and closes issues; for anyone else those become proposals. cr2-build stays a project skill in the cr2 repo. Skill count 15 -> 19. PRIOR HISTORY: Chalette internal dev & QA toolkit for Command Room. v0.5.1 (2026-07-29) — REFGAP1: cross-skill-interaction-test's three cited reference docs recovered + a permanent dangling-reference guard. The bug, found live at the v5.5.1 attended gate: SKILL.md Step 1 loads references/sequence-catalog.md (plus temporal-wait-strategy.md and multi-phase-verdict-aggregation.md), but git tracked only SKILL.md — the references/ directory existed and was EMPTY, so the skill failed on a missing file even with a valid operator profile. Recovery finding: the files never existed anywhere — chalette-dev, chalette030, and retired-plugin git history never tracked them and no session transcript contains a write of them; BUILD_VCRRETIRE §7 had already recorded all three inside a 13-citation dangling-read set across five skills and deferred the guard to its own build. This is that build. The three docs were authored from SKILL.md's own inline content: the catalog carries all 17 index rows (original 15 + the two OBJ1 sequences), with the Bug #51 cascade sequence READY and every derived entry DRAFT under an explicit promotion rule (walk once, confirm expected substrate writes, promote to READY; DRAFT failures report ADVISORY, never blocking — an unverified draft expectation cannot assert a phantom regression). Expected-write event names checked against cr1's events.schema.json; pulse and the commitments task are flagged as scheduled surfaces rather than skills; the weekly-audit row's surface is noted as now living in cleanup; each file carries a provenance header so nobody hunts a lost original again. Guard 4 added (tests/test_reference_integrity.py), the instruction-layer-gap class inverted from G13: every references/*.md a SKILL.md cites must be git-TRACKED (untracked is absent at client install), present on disk, and non-empty. Bare citations resolve against the citing skill; prefixed other-skill/references/ citations resolve against the named skill when it exists in this repo; cross-repo citations (command-room/… lives in cr1, verified present there) are skipped as outside CI's jurisdiction. The 8 remaining pre-existing dangling citations (bug-regression-suite x2, ship-readiness-gate x3, skill-generator x2, skill-creator's mis-citation of a checklist that actually lives under cr-skill-builder/references/) are grandfathered in a baseline that RATCHETS BOTH WAYS: a new dangling citation fails immediately, and fixing a grandfathered one without deleting its baseline row also fails, so a stale row cannot mask a re-regression. Coverage asserted, not assumed: the scan must visit every skill's SKILL.md, with three controls — positive (the three repaired citations resolve tracked), negative (a fabricated citation registers as dangling), and a misattribution pin (a prefixed citation resolves to its OWNER, not the citing skill — the exact false-dangling the naive resolver produced during this build). Mutation-verified both directions: untracking the catalog went 2 red, satisfying a baseline entry went ratchet-red, restored green. Battery 59 -> 65 passed; Guard 1 OK 15/20/0. Deliberately NOT done: authoring the 8 grandfathered docs (each belongs to its owning skill's build, with review) and any SKILL.md text change — all frontmatter descriptions untouched repo-wide, zero trigger changes. Skill count unchanged (15). PRIOR HISTORY: Chalette internal dev & QA toolkit for Command Room. v0.5.0 (2026-07-27) — GATE1: build authority decoupled from may_ship. A contractor can now write a spec and build from it in one continuous pass, with review happening ONCE at the pull request — and still hold ZERO ship authority. Root cause: may_ship conflated three distinct authorities (may I build from a spec I wrote myself / may I bump the version + write CHANGELOG + cut a release / may I promote to client repos) and there was no key for the first, so it rode may_ship by implication. New operator key may_build_own_spec splits it out. It SHIPS TRUE — the one authority key that does. The spec ruled it overlay-only with a committed false, matching the other two; M overruled that on the call: an overlay is a hand-created gitignored file, so the grant would have been invisible to git pull, absent on a fresh clone, and silently lost on a re-clone — a forgettable setup step guarding something a PR review already catches. Shipping it on makes a plain git pull the entire setup. The cost taken knowingly: the value travels with the repo, so a future contributor inherits build authority instead of being granted it one at a time; with two collaborators on a private repo and may_ship / may_promote / allowed_targets all still shipping locked, that is a small price. Consequence recorded in three places: contractor-safe now means zero SHIP authority and synthetic targets only, not zero authority. This had to be a code change and not a verbal agreement: the pre-build gate was prose inside triage-intake/SKILL.md, and prose re-asserts itself on every run — the next triage session would have read 'contractors never self-approve a spec into a build' and asked for the handoff again regardless of what was agreed on a call (the instruction-layer-drift class). Two sentences re-gated in skills/triage-intake/SKILL.md: the operator-aware blockquote now lists may_build_own_spec and states the two authorities separately instead of one implying the other (may_ship: false spells out what it withholds — version bump, CHANGELOG, release, promote, self-merge — and binds regardless of the build grant); the 'Writing the spec' delivery rule moves off may_ship onto may_build_own_spec, so a granted profile lands its spec in specs_dir ready to build REGARDLESS of may_ship with the PR as the review point, while an ungranted profile keeps the previous hand-it-over behaviour verbatim. Deliberate deviation from the spec: the granted branch fires on may_build_own_spec true OR may_ship true — re-gating on the new key alone would have regressed M's own flow, because his overlay predates the key and would have fallen through to the committed false, telling the maintainer to hand his own specs over. Explicitly NOT changed: 'Routing work out' (contributor packets + the cr1 BACKLOG.md) stays gated on may_ship because routing work OUT to other people is genuinely a ship-operator function and a contractor does not route work to themselves; the three may_ship references in references/spec-templates.md; the Writer contract's ship/promote line; cr-test's tier-5 may_ship (a different concept); allowed_targets, which stays ['synthetic'] — this grants build authority, not real-workspace access; may_promote. The triage-intake frontmatter description is byte-identical, so zero trigger changes and no G11 budget impact — body text only. Guard 2 pins may_build_own_spec == TRUE, which runs the opposite direction from its two neighbours on purpose: it is not a safety fence but a do-not-silently-take-it-away fence, because a revert to false sends every contractor back to the pre-build handoff with no error and no clue why. The real safety fences (may_ship, may_promote, allowed_targets, workspace_root, scrub_roster) still pin the locked values and are untouched. Mutation-verified both ways against the shipped value (reverted to false: 1 failed / 49 passed; assertion then removed with the bad value still in place: 49 passed, proving only the fence caught it). Guard 3 gains three instruction-layer fences on the new delivery rule, which can fail in BOTH directions — narrowed back to may_ship (the handoff silently returns) or widened to no gate (every profile self-approves its own specs); mutation-verified 3 red on drift-back, 1 red on a deleted false-branch, 1 red on a deleted does-not-grant-ship-authority sentence, and green once the fences themselves are removed. Battery 50 passed / 9 skipped. README gains a plain-English What-you-can-and-cannot-do table covering all four authority keys and what each ships as, and setup step 3 now says explicitly that there is nothing to create or turn on — under the spec original overlay-only design nothing would have told Eric the key existed, since the docs said only M keeps an overlay. CLAUDE.md carries a three-row authority table and the honest note that these keys are a coordination contract, not a security boundary — the boundary is GitHub access (read-only on cr1, fork to PR, M merges). Accepted tradeoff: Eric now rules his own §0 AWAIT rows, so a rejected APPROACH at PR time wastes the whole build; the agreed middle ground is a one-line heads-up on architecture-shaping calls, no gate. Same-class sweep: nine SKILL.md files carried the parenthetical only-M-has-one claim about config/operator.local.json, false the moment a contractor keeps an overlay; swept to not-every-operator-has-one across bug-regression-suite, capture-for-code, cr-skill-builder, cr-test, cross-skill-interaction-test, scale-stress-test, ship-readiness-gate, smoke-watch and triage-intake. Deliberately excluded and verified unchanged: operator.json _comment_chalette_clone (that one is about a chalette030 clone and is still true) and this description field (a historical chain — history is not rewritten to match the present). Zero trigger changes proven not asserted: all nine frontmatter descriptions compared byte-for-byte against HEAD, 9 same / 0 changed. Skill count unchanged (15). PRIOR HISTORY: Chalette internal dev & QA toolkit for Command Room. v0.4.1 (2026-07-27) — VCRRETIRE: verify-cr-release retired; tier 5 becomes the dogfood ritual, walked by hand. M's ruling (2026-07-25): dogfood-before-promote plus BIG-TEST carry the attended layer, so the paste-back orchestrator's state tracking, prompt-rotation templates, phase-decision gates, and verdict-doc generation are ceremony no longer run. What the skill OWNED was kept, not deleted — three reference docs moved to their real owners with git mv so history follows the file: VERIFICATION_PLAN.md to cr-test/references/ (cr-test owns tier 5, and the plan was always a repo-level asset — line 3 always said 'the plan Eric maintains'), response-classifier.md and findings-log-format.md to bug-regression-suite/references/ (that skill fires prompts and classifies responses — step 3 of its own procedure). Both relocated shared docs gained a 'shared asset — sweep the citers before moving' header so the next retirement does not re-orphan them. Tier 5 is now stated as explicitly TWO halves, and cr-test refuses to call it covered on dogfood alone: freeform dogfood runs on a mature real workspace and therefore CANNOT reach virgin-workspace onboarding, honest empty states, the Phase-3 destructive probes, late-fire behavior, or the fresh-runtime loader canary — only the structured plan against a fresh, empty workspace does. CLAUDE.md and README.md grew a Track C to match; the two-track framing had no slot for the plan. Orphaned triggers re-homed: 'verify cr release' / 'run verification suite' alias 'cr test --attended', 'pre-ship check' aliases 'cr test --ship' (no collision with ship-readiness-gate's own 'pre-promote check'); 'continue verification' / 'resume verification' are deliberately DROPPED — they resumed a stateful session that no longer exists, and re-homing them would promise a resumption nothing provides. The two DOES-NOT-FIRE fences that pointed at the dead skill now name where the phrases actually go; left as-was they would have told those skills not to fire on phrases NO skill owned. ship-readiness-gate's ~80/20 coverage claim was CORRECTED rather than quietly dropped: the 20% is still addressable at the same attended tier but is no longer enforced — nothing tracks position through the plan, auto-classifies responses, or emits a verdict artifact — so the gate now carries two consequences: never infer the attended tier from a PROMOTE, and make the operator state what was actually walked ('attended: dogfood only, plan not walked' is a legitimate verdict-doc line). Silence is not coverage. Skill count 16 -> 15. PRIOR HISTORY: Chalette internal dev & QA toolkit for Command Room. v0.4.0 (2026-07-24) — TI2: triage-intake gains a route-work-out mode. On a may_ship operator profile ONLY, an item whose triage verdict is SPEC and which passes the five-clause contributor-suitability test (target repo is cr1; fully specifiable from repo contents; buildable and testable against the battery + synthetic fixtures alone; zero client/org/person names needed anywhere including PR text; zero ship authority) now yields two additional outputs: a self-contained packet at <specs_dir>/packets/PACKET_<TAG>.md that a cold fork contributor can execute without the maintainer online (handoff header, a spec body shaped per cr1's checked-in templates/TEMPLATE_SPEC.md with §0 already ruled, kickoff prompt, acceptance incl. the scrub AC verbatim, and an explicit PR-description-requirements block carrying the TEMPLATE_BUILD_REPORT slots), and one scrubbed READY row staged onto a repo-root BACKLOG.md in the cr1 clone that the contributor can read from their fork. Both outbound surfaces pass a FAIL-CLOSED scrub gate first: the new scrub_roster operator key (committed default null, real value overlay-only) is grepped against the full outbound text, and a null/unreadable roster REFUSES both writes with an explicit reason line rather than emitting unscrubbed text — the org-name-leak class cannot ride cr1's G9 alone, whose first-name dictionary cannot know real ORG names. BACKLOG writes are STAGE-AND-SHOW: git add + show the staged diff in the closing decision table, then stop — a triage session ends with zero new commits in the cr1 clone, and the maintainer pushes in his own ship window. The closing decision table gains an Eric? column. Zero trigger changes: the frontmatter description is byte-identical to v0.3.1, both features are inert behind the may_ship gate on a contractor profile, and INTAKE1 F1/F5 are untouched. Skill count unchanged (16). PRIOR HISTORY: Chalette internal dev & QA toolkit for Command Room. v0.3.1 (2026-07-24) — MAINT2: maintenance batch. (1) FIX: the operator-profile resolution pattern no longer silently no-ops under Git Bash on Windows (SHIP_RECORD_CONSOL2 finding 3, pattern-wide across all 11 reading skills). The bash blocks built the plugin root from ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} — empty when an agent runs a SKILL.md block through a Bash tool — and from pwd, which yields an MSYS path (/c/Users/...) that native python.exe resolves to C:\c\Users\..., so BOTH config reads missed, the merged profile came back empty, and every skill fell through to its synthetic default with no error: an operator granted allowed_targets [real] silently ran synthetic. The canonical preamble now searches for config/operator.json (with a $CHALETTE_DEV_ROOT escape hatch, never a hardcoded machine path), converts with cygpath -m, and FAILS LOUD on an unreadable root or profile; the python-form skills carry the same loud fence plus the native-path contract for SKILL_PLUGIN_ROOT. Guard 2 gains Fence 4 (+29 tests, 24 -> 53; 51 after the two retirements drop their quick_validate cases): the shipped preamble is EXECUTED out of each SKILL.md and asserted to read a non-empty profile, mutation-verified both ways. (2) RETIRED compare-canonical-vs-freelance — its niche (validating the v3.13.8 §3.6 canonical-vs-freelance widget ladder per skill) is closed; the freelance fallback it diffed against no longer exists, and synthetic invariant I2 (no_freelance_render) asserts the property the diff was inferring; ship-readiness-gate's coverage claims were corrected rather than inherited (Bug #48 action-label drift is cr1's CanonicalActionError validator in the unit tier, not this gate). (3) FOLDED run-command-room-tests into cr-test — it never had a delegating caller, and its hardcoded five suites were long superseded by tests/run_all.py's call-time discovery; its trigger phrases ('internal: run plugin tests', 'run command room tests', 'command room health check', 'verify plugin code') are now aliases for 'cr test --quick' in cr-test's description. Skill count 18 -> 16. PRIOR HISTORY: Chalette internal dev & QA toolkit for Command Room. v0.3.0 (2026-07-24) — CONSOL1: chalette-dev becomes the SINGLE canonical home of the shared QA/dev toolkit; the duplicate copies were removed from the private chalette plugin (which drifted). The 18 skills were reconciled to their canonical, operator-fenced form (newest-wins WITH fence preservation): operator profile gains chalette_clone / specs_dir / parking_doc keys plus a gitignored config/operator.local.json overlay — M's real-workspace profile lives ONLY in that overlay; the committed operator.json stays the contractor-safe default. ship-readiness-gate rebuilt on the operator pattern (default synthetic; real only when allowed_targets grants it); synthetic-workspace-runtime-test re-adds the event_gate_routed invariant (D6); triage-intake carries INTAKE1 F5 (resurrection guard, ported from chalette030) + F4 (chalette_clone, operator-aware) + specs_dir/parking_doc/may_ship-gated delivery; capture-for-code scopes its placeholder-names rule to non-real operators (F7); all real-path and M-identity leaks fenced.
